shippingNews.postTitle: McCarthy Takes Final Coal Load from SMET Dock

stories.body: Walter J. McCarthy Jr. loading the last coal cargo at SMET on Saturday as Mesabi Miner backs toward the ore dock. [Scott Bjorklund] SUPERIOR, WI – The final vessel has departed with coal from the Midwest Energy Terminal in Superior, bringing a half-century of major fossil fuel transshipment on the Twin Ports waterfront to an official close. On Friday night, the 1,000-foot bulk carrier Walter J. McCarthy Jr. passed beneath the Duluth Aerial Lift Bridge to take on the terminal's concluding cargo before operations cease permanently. She departed mid-evening Saturday for the lower lakes. Built in

shippingNews.postTitle: Bulk Carrier Hits Docked Tanker at Montreal

stories.body: MONTREAL, QC – The bulk carrier Federal Beaufort arriving at the Port of Montreal Friday afternoon from downstream, reportedly struck the tanker Hinch Spirit, which was stationary and moored alongside at Section 35 while receiving bunkers. The Hinch Spirit reportedly sustained damage to her port quarter and starboard side, while the Federal Beaufort sustained damage to her bow. No injuries have been reported. Both vessels are currently moored alongside, awaiting divers and an investigation by Transport Canada. Janey Anderson – Ship Junkies - Lakes, Locks & Rivers (LL&R)

shippingNews.postTitle: R/V Neil Armstrong Fuels in Detroit on Her Way to Duluth

stories.body: DETROIT, MI – The oceanographic research vessel Neil Armstrong stopped in Detroit Friday to fuel. By 9 p.m. she was headed upriver and will pass Port Huron in the dark. todayInHistory.title: Fire Causes Significant Damage to Two Harbors Lighthouse Gift Shop
todayInHistory.text: TWO HARBORS, MN – An investigation is underway after a detached building that’s used as a gift shop for the Two Harbors Lighthouse went up in flames Monday evening. As of Tuesday morning, local authorities have yet to release information on the blaze, which likely broke out around 5:30 p.m. Officials with the Lake County Historical Society, which controls the lakeside property, told Northern News Now that no one was injured, but the damage to the building is significant. “We were literally watching a piece of Lake County’s history go up in those flames,” Lake County Historical Society Vice President David Johnson said in an interview with the station. It’s believed that the fire started in the breezeway between the gift shop and a connected structure, both of which are separate from the historic lighthouse. The Lake County Historical Society shared this statement: “We are incredibly grateful to the firefighters and first responders who have responded and are working to address the situation. Their time, dedication, and efforts are greatly appreciated.” Bring Me The News Gift shop fire at Two Harbors Lighthouse.

marineWeather.synopsis: 29.5 inch low pressure moving over northern Ontario extends a 29.7 inch trough over the lake this morning. This low gets absorbed into a 29.3 inch low over the Canadian Maritimes this evening, allowing 30.0 inch ridging to return over Lake Superior tonight. By Monday morning, a 29.6 inch low will move over Lake Winnipeg, weakening to 29.7 inches as it moves over northern Ontario and brings 29.8 inch troughing over Lake Superior Monday night. This trough shifts east to Quebec Tuesday through Wednesday as 30.4 inch high pressure builds over Manitoba and Ontario. This high slowly descends southeast, reaching western Lake Superior at 30.2 inches Friday.
marineWeather.warning: GALE WARNING IN EFFECT UNTIL 10 PM EST THIS EVENING

marineWeather.synopsis: Low pressure of 29.5 inches crossing Ontario is dragging a weak cold front south through Lake Michigan, shifting winds from southwest to west-northwest. Winds are expected to strengthen behind this front, bringing gusts around 30 kt. Winds will diminish tonight as a ridge of high pressure around 30.1 inches moves into the region. Winds become southwesterly again on Monday as an additional low pressure system moves through the Canadian Prairies. Winds will shift northwesterly Monday night as low pressure exits into Ontario and another cold front sweeps across the Upper Great Lakes. Winds then shift westerly Tuesday into Tuesday night before turning northerly as low pressure deepens in the Southeast U.S. on Wednesday. Wednesday into Thursday, expect a strong band of lake effect snow and rain to develop north to south as low pressure deepens to 29.4 inches as it crosses Indiana and Ohio. Northerly gales are possible on Thursday.

Low pressure, 29.50 inches, clips the northern Great Lakes this evening into early Monday, pushing a cold front down across the region. This brings some additional showers to the central Great Lakes with a period of elevated winds/waves. The strongest wind are expected later this afternoon into Monday morning, when northwest winds prevail behind the cold front. Drier conditions expected early next week.

marineWeather.synopsis: A ridge averaging 30.10 inches will build over the lake today. Another cold front will sweep southeast across the lake Sunday night with a trough averaging 30.00 inches persisting early next week.

A 29.2 inch low will move slowly north across the Canadian Maritimes today through Monday, with a secondary cold front moving southeast across the lake tonight. A 30.2 inch high will then build from the lower Ohio Valley Monday to off the southeast coast Tuesday and Wednesday. A 29.4 inch low is then forecast to move into the Ohio Valley Wednesday night, then move across Pennsylvania and New York Thursday. A secondary coastal low is then expected to develop off the New England coast and deepen to 29.2 inches Friday through Saturday as it spins over the Gulf of Maine.
